1: # Instructions
2: 
3: Reparent a tree on a selected node.
4: 
5: A [tree][wiki-tree] is a special type of [graph][wiki-graph] where all nodes are connected but there are no cycles.
6: That means, there is exactly one path to get from one node to another for any pair of nodes.
7: 
8: This exercise is all about re-orientating a tree to see things from a different point of view.
9: For example family trees are usually presented from the ancestor's perspective:
10: 
11: ```text
12:     +------0------+
13:     |      |      |
14:   +-1-+  +-2-+  +-3-+
15:   |   |  |   |  |   |
16:   4   5  6   7  8   9
17: ```
18: 
19: But there is no inherent direction in a tree.
20: The same information can be presented from the perspective of any other node in the tree, by pulling it up to the root and dragging its relationships along with it.
21: So the same tree from 6's perspective would look like:
22: 
23: ```text
24:         6
25:         |
26:   +-----2-----+
27:   |           |
28:   7     +-----0-----+
29:         |           |
30:       +-1-+       +-3-+
31:       |   |       |   |
32:       4   5       8   9
33: ```
34: 
35: This lets us more simply describe the paths between two nodes.
36: So for example the path from 6-9 (which in the first tree goes up to the root and then down to a different leaf node) can be seen to follow the path 6-2-0-3-9.
37: 
38: This exercise involves taking an input tree and re-orientating it from the point of view of one of the nodes.
39: 
40: [wiki-graph]: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tree_(graph_theory)
41: [wiki-tree]: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Graph_(discrete_mathematics)

Done. All 15 tests in `pov_test.py` pass, and I verified the implementation doesn't mutate the input tree.

## What I implemented in `pov.py`

Two public methods plus a few private helpers:

- **`from_pov(from_node)`** — finds the path from the root to `from_node`; if it doesn't exist, raises `ValueError("Tree could not be reoriented")`. Otherwise it rebuilds the tree so `from_node` is the root.
- **`path_to(from_node, to_node)`** — if `to_node` doesn't exist, raises `ValueError("No path found")`. Otherwise it re-roots at `from_node` and walks down to `to_node`, returning the list of labels. (A missing source surfaces as the `from_pov` error, matching the test expectations.)

The core of the re-orientation (`_reorient`) walks the root→target path and rebuilds the "parent chain" from the root down: each ancestor keeps its off-path children and gains the already-built chain as a child, so the original root ends up deepest. The target then keeps its own children and gets that chain appended. The key subtlety I handled: building the chain **root→target** (not target→root) so the target's former parent sits nearest the new root, and deep-copying side subtrees so the original tree is never mutated.

The existing dunder methods (`__dict__`, `__eq__`, etc.) were left untouched — `__eq__` compares via a child-sorted dict, so child ordering doesn't affect equality. No new files were created.
